newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cypriot denies infecting Briton with AIDS.
newsitem.headline: Cypriot denies infecting Briton with AIDS.

text.p: A Greek Cypriot fisherman on Friday pleaded not guilty to charges of infecting his former British lover with the life-threatening AIDS disease.
Briton Janette Pink, who has developed full-blown AIDS, is due to testify in court on May 22 against Pavlos Georgiou, her ex-boyfriend who has the HIV virus that leads to AIDS.

Georgiou, 40, from the southeastern resort of Ayia Napa, is accused of negligently infecting Pink with the virus while knowing he was a carrier during an affair in Cyprus between September 1993 and January 1996.

Pink, from Basildon, Essex, has accused Georgiou of failing to tell her about his condition during their affair. She also says he concealed the death of his wife from acquired immune deficiency syndrome (AIDS).
The 44-year-old divorced mother of two is now said to be seriously ill with doctors giving her just a few years to live, according to British newspaper reports.
The charges against Georgiou carry a maximum prison sentence of two years, a 1,500 Cyprus pound ($2,950) fine, or both.
Georgiou, a bespectacled bearded father of four with no obvious signs of illness, shook his head and said "no" in Greek when asked by police prosecutor Sotiris Kokkinou if he admitted to the charge.
The case is the first legal test in Cyprus on how to handle allegations that a carrier of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) has recklessly or deliberately passed on the virus to another person.
It prompted district judge Antonis Liatsos to issue an appeal to the media present in court that coverage of the case avoid "stigmatising" the accused.

"The court expects there to be freedom of information on the one hand and that on the other, the accused receive the correct treatment on the media's part ... having in mind that he himself faces a serious problem," Liatsos said.
He ordered that Georgiou be released on a 1,000 pound bail and hand his travel documents over to the authorities until the date of the hearing.
